title: BIGStudent2.0 - Effect of bitter gourd (Momordica charantia) on the blood glucose curve after oral maltodextrin intake
summary: Bittergourd is an Asian vegetable and is known in traditional medicine in many regions for its positive effects on diabetes and blood sugar levels. There are different mechanisms through which bittergourd can regulate blood sugar levels. One possibility is the reduced breakdown and absorption of complex sugars from the gut. This study aims to investigate whether 2.5 g of dried bittergourd powder can reduce the blood sugar spike in healthy adults after consuming 75 g of carbohydrates. Four different treatments will be compared: i) bittergourd with lemon juice, water, and 75 g of carbohydrates from maltodextrin, ii) bittergourd with lemon juice, oat drink, and 75 g of carbohydrates from the oat drink and maltodextrin, as well as the two respective control drinks with cucumber powder instead of bittergourd powder. Blood sugar levels are measured from capillary blood from the finger before and for 2 hours after taking a test drink and compared between treatments. In addition, blood pressure is measured, and questionnaires are used to ask about how participants feel and the taste of the drinks.

interventions.name: Intake of 75 g of maltodextrin with 2.5 g of cucumber and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 300 mL of water, and measurement of capillary blood glucose concentrations before and every 15 minutes for 120 minutes after intake.

Intake of 75 g of maltodextrin with 2.5 g of bitter gourd and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 300 mL of water, and measurement of capillary blood glucose concentrations before and every 15 minutes for 120 minutes after intake.

Intake of 53.7 g of maltodextrin with 2.5 g of bitter gourd and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 300 mL of oat drink, and measurement of capillary blood glucose concentrations before and every 15 minutes for 120 minutes after intake.

Intake of 53.7 g of maltodextrin with 2.5 g of cucumber and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 300 mL of oat drink, and measurement of capillary blood glucose concentrations before and every 15 minutes for 120 minutes after intake.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Voluntary participation confirmed with signature; according to their own statements, healthy students of the modules BP167, MP006, and BP182, as well as the members of the Nutrition in Prevention and Therapy working group at the Institute of Nutritional Science at JLU Giessen; BMI >17.5 to 29.9 kg/m²
Exclusion criteria:
Allergy to oats or lemon/citrus fruits; known diabetes mellitus, taking medications for blood sugar; taking medications that affect blood sugar or blood pressure; chronic gastrointestinal diseases; pregnancy, breastfeeding; general low-carb diet; low-carb diet in the last 3 days before the test; heavy alcohol consumption the night before the examination; bleeding disorder, fear of blood
